title: Explainability-Aided Monitoring: Importing XAI from IDS for Human-Interpretable AI Safety Alerts
original_idea: Train anomaly detector (isolation forest/one-class SVM) on benign trajectories. Apply SHAP to anomaly scores on SHADE-Arena trajectories to identify contributing features. Evaluate whether SHAP explanations match ground-truth malicious actions. Conduct small user study (5 participants).

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Clear theory: explainable alerts improve human oversight effectiveness. The causal chain from XAI to better human decisions is well-documented in IDS literature and directly relevant to AI safety.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires training an anomaly detector, applying SHAP (which can be finicky), AND conducting a user study. The user study alone adds significant complexity (IRB considerations, study design, participant recruitment). Challenging for beginners in 30hrs.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Three distinct components: (1) train anomaly detector, (2) apply SHAP and evaluate, (3) user study. Each is a project on its own. The user study especially broadens scope significantly. Too much for 30hrs.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Novelty not assessed due to partial Wave 3 completion.
